maya: kicking off a post-rollout load test now. goal: reproduce the 2x tail-latency regression we saw after the kernel selector change. running both synthetic and replay harnesses.
jon: thanks — which nodes/pool? dedicated pool or shared hosted?
maya: starting on a small dedicated pool (dpool-qa-3) to be safe, will also spin up a hosted burst test after.
li: quick note: kernel change switched default GEMM path for 16k sequences, might affect cold KV warmup.
eric: can you save the profiler trace and the kernel selection log? add --record-kernel-decisions to the harness.
maya: yep logging that. harness config pasted: ```harness --mode=synth --rps=800 --p50=20ms --p95-target=300ms --replay-file=recent-prod.json --record-kernel-decisions --kv-cache=true```
perf-bot: baseline snapshot attached: perf/baseline/1766980000 (size: 1.4MB)
maya: initial synth run shows p95 jumps at t=120s when autoscaler kicks in. scale-up time ~48s measured from first queued request to new replica online.
jon: 48s seems high — our target is <30s for that pool. are we seeing cold-start compile overheads?
li: checking kernel logs — when new replica starts, it chooses xformers kernels and performs a tiny JIT for fused attention; compile step ~12s on GPU0.
maya: adding profiler sample around the 12s: ```TRACE: compile:fused_attn:11.6s, init_kv_map:2.1s, warm_caches:6.9s```
eric: warm_caches 6.9s looks like KV cache population step, but that should be near-zero for cold starts. are we prefetching KV from persistent cache?
li: yes, we added a prefetch optimization that tries to hydrate prefix caches from disk for recent sessions — if disk is slow it stalls. on the dedicated pool the SSD I/O was saturated by parallel booting.
sre-oncall: observed burst-credit depletion on that pool at t=110s, which throttled instance boot throughput. logs: "burst_credits=0, pending_boots=4"
junior: (small note) synth traffic ramps at 200rps/min, maybe too aggressive; replay run is more spiky and matched production pattern better.
maya: ran replay harness with same initial conditions; interestingly, p95 didn't spike as badly and scale-up happened in ~32s. looks like synthetic steady ramp creates a queueing pattern that triggers multiple simultaneous boots and hits burst credit limit.
eric: apples-to-apples: we should run synth with production-shaped ramp (sawtooth + pauses). also add per-replica stagger of 3s to avoid concurrent cold-starts.
li: on kernel selection side, when many requests backlog, the selector aggressively picks lower-accuracy kernels that are faster but increase variance in per-token latencies due to micro-batching. might be compounding the tail.
maya: quick experiment: forced kernel_override=low_variance for new replicas and re-ran synth ramp with stagger. result: p95 reduced from 420ms -> 260ms, scale-up time unchanged but overall tail smaller.
jon: that sounds promising. low_variance kernels trade raw throughput for predictability which is good for p95 SLAs. we should document trade-offs and expose per-pool default kernel profiles.
eric: also we should tune batching heuristics: current dynamic_batcher increases max_batch_size to chase throughput under backlog which spikes memory usage and triggers GC-like stalls on CPU for KV map resizing. observed 150ms GC pauses in host process.
li: KV cache behavior note: when memory threshold hits 85%, cache eviction runs and causes short pauses while rebuilding hash tables — happened at t=135s during synth. might need incremental eviction.
sre-oncall: ops idea: for dedicated pools, reserve burst credits and stagger instance boots via orchestration; and add a cold-start fast-path binary that skips prefetch on boot and warms asynchronously.
maya: plan: 1) reproduce using production-shaped synth load, 2) run with and without kernel_override to capture diffs, 3) add stagger window and reserved burst credits, 4) capture profiler traces and kernel-decision logs for both synth and replay.
jon: please post a short summary of diffs (p50/p95/scale-up) once you have runs. also include exact harness flags and node metrics (IOPS, burst credits, mem).
maya: will do. uploading first run artifacts to perf bucket: gs://redwood-perf/postrollout/1767001234/{synth1, replay1, kernel_logs}. tarballs include `kernel.decisions.log`, `perf.trace`, `node-metrics.csv`.
eric: one more ask: add a small micro-benchmark that triggers only the kernel compile path (no KV) so we can isolate compile time variance.
li: created microbench command: ```./bench_compile --model small --seq=16384 --iter=5 --record=compile.trace``` — running now.
maya: thanks team. next sync in #eng-runtime tomorrow with numbers. :thumbsup:
